appearance_facts.fact: Vertical color legend with a white-to-dark-maroon gradient; tick labels 100, 80, 60, 40, 20, 0.
New York (NY) is filled with the darkest maroon, matching the extreme 'High' end of the legend.
Kentucky (KY), Illinois (IL), Ohio (OH), Tennessee (TN) are dark red/maroon, near the high end.
Texas (TX) is a strong red, high but visibly lighter than NY.
Delaware (DE) is a light orange/tan, mid-low on the scale.
North Carolina (NC) is pale yellow, near the 'Low' end of the scale.
Washington (WA) is dark red/maroon, high; Oregon (OR) is medium red.
Several states (CA, AZ, NM, CO, AR, AL, RI, ME partial) are gray, indicating no data.

printed_facts.fact: Title: 'Prevalence of Species Z in Each State'.
Legend bottom label '0 High' (dark maroon); scale runs 100, 80, 60, 40, 20, 0.
State label 'NY' in darkest maroon (highest prevalence band).
State label 'NC' in pale yellow (low prevalence band).
State label 'DE' in light orange (mid-low band).
State label 'TX' in strong red (high band, below NY).
State label 'WA' in dark red/maroon (high band).

public_definitions: Routing criterion: 'Highest prevalence state in the dashboard'.
chart_reference: 'Use the state prevalence dashboard as the evidence source for selecting the highest-prevalence state record.'
Option: 'Open New York (NY) prevalence detail for priority follow-up'.
uncertain: No numeric prevalence values are printed per state; ranking relies on color-band comparison against the legend.

The legend is inverted (100=Low at top, 0=High at bottom), so the darkest maroon corresponds to the highest prevalence; exact ordering among the darkest states (NY vs WA vs KY/IL) is not numerically resolvable from the image.
